questions.prompt: A hospital is choosing between technetium-99m (half-life 6 hours, gamma emitter) and iodine-131 (half-life 8 days, beta and gamma emitter) for thyroid imaging. Evaluate the physics factors that should inform this choice.

levels.title: Level 3 (High Mark Band)
levels.ao1: Comprehensive, accurate technical knowledge using correct terminology throughout.
levels.ao2: Thorough application to the scenario with coherent, logical progression of ideas.
levels.ao3: Critical, balanced evaluation; arguments substantiated and a reasoned conclusion drawn.

levels.title: Level 2 (Medium Mark Band)
levels.ao1: Sound knowledge of concepts with mostly correct terminology.
levels.ao2: Application to the context is present but uneven or partially developed.
levels.ao3: Some evaluation; arguments one-sided or conclusions asserted rather than reasoned.

levels.title: Level 1 (Low Mark Band)
levels.ao1: Basic knowledge; isolated facts or terminology with occasional inaccuracy.
levels.ao2: Superficial or generic application; little reference to the actual scenario.
levels.ao3: Little or no evaluation; opinion without justification.

indicativeContent: Half-life: short enough to limit patient dose, long enough to complete imaging
Radiation type: gamma escapes the body for detection; beta is absorbed internally increasing dose
Ionisation density — beta more damaging per absorption
Energy of emitted gamma must suit the camera detection efficiency
Excretion/biological half-life interacts with physical half-life
Balanced conclusion justifying technetium-99m's dominance in diagnostic imaging

questions.prompt: A student plans an experiment to determine the resistivity of a nichrome wire using a micrometer, a metre rule, an ammeter and a voltmeter. Describe how the experiment should be carried out and evaluate how the design minimises the uncertainty in the final value of resistivity.

levels.title: Level 3 (High Mark Band)
levels.ao1: Comprehensive accurate knowledge: logically structured method plus sustained evaluation of uncertainty reduction.
levels.ao2: Fully sustained, logically structured application to the scenario.
levels.ao3: Balanced, well-justified evaluation reaching a supported conclusion.

levels.title: Level 2 (Medium Mark Band)
levels.ao1: Sound knowledge: coherent method with correct measurements and some treatment of uncertainty.
levels.ao2: Applies the physics to the scenario with mostly coherent reasoning.
levels.ao3: Some evaluation, though uneven or incomplete.

levels.title: Level 1 (Low Mark Band)
levels.ao1: Limited accurate knowledge: fragments of method with no uncertainty awareness.

indicativeContent: Measure diameter with the micrometer at several positions and orientations along the wire; average to reduce random error
Measure length with the metre rule; contact resistance at crocodile clips is a systematic concern
Record V and I for several lengths or use a rheostat for multiple pairs; plot R against L
Resistivity ρ = RA/L: the gradient of the R–L graph multiplied by cross-sectional area A = πd²/4
Graph-gradient technique reduces the impact of zero errors compared with single-point calculation
Keep current low/short-lived to avoid heating — resistance rises with temperature, biasing ρ
Percentage uncertainty dominated by diameter because it enters as d²

questions.prompt: A civil engineer designs a banked curve for a motorway. Explain, with reference to the forces acting on a vehicle, how banking allows the curve to be taken without friction at a design speed, and evaluate what happens when vehicles travel significantly faster or slower than this speed.

levels.title: Level 3 (High Mark Band)
levels.ao1: Comprehensive accurate knowledge: full analysis with tan θ = v²/(rg) and evaluation of off-design-speed behaviour.
levels.ao2: Fully sustained, logically structured application to the scenario.
levels.ao3: Balanced, well-justified evaluation reaching a supported conclusion.

levels.title: Level 2 (Medium Mark Band)
levels.ao1: Sound knowledge: correctly resolves weight and normal reaction, identifying the horizontal component as centripetal.
levels.ao2: Applies the physics to the scenario with mostly coherent reasoning.
levels.ao3: Some evaluation, though uneven or incomplete.

levels.title: Level 1 (Low Mark Band)
levels.ao1: Limited accurate knowledge: mentions centripetal force without correct force analysis.

indicativeContent: On a banked track the normal reaction tilts toward the centre; its horizontal component supplies centripetal force
At design speed no friction is needed: N sin θ = mv²/r and N cos θ = mg, giving tan θ = v²/(rg)
Faster than design speed: friction acts down the slope adding centripetal force; insufficient friction means sliding outward
Slower: friction acts up the slope preventing the vehicle sliding inward
Design depends on radius and speed only — mass cancels, so all vehicles share the same design speed
Real design includes a friction margin, so the banking angle is a compromise across conditions
